14	/-!
15	# Zariski descent of representability (`thm:representability_zariski_descent`)
16	
17	This file proves **Zariski descent of representability** (EGA 0_I 4.5.4;
18	cf. Stacks 01JJ): a presheaf `F : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type 1` satisfying the Zariski
19	sheaf axiom (`Scheme.IsZariskiSheafOver`, stated against open covers of the
20	total space of each `T : Over S`) that is representable over every member of
21	an open cover of `S` is representable by an `S`-scheme
22	(`Scheme.representable_of_openCover`).
23	
24	The definitions `overRes` / `overResHom` / `overResLE` / `IsZariskiSheafOver`
25	and the statement of the descent theorem previously lived in
26	`GrassmannianRepresentability.lean` (where the theorem was a typed `sorry`
27	leaf); they are moved here so the Grassmannian file can consume the proof.
28	
29	## Proof architecture
30	
31	The heavy gluing content (cocycle conditions, `Scheme.GlueData`, the
32	locally-bijective sheaf comparison) is **not** redone by hand: it is delegated
33	to mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy`
34	(Stacks 01JJ), which applies to a `Type 0`-valued Zariski *sheaf* on the
35	absolute category `Scheme.{0}` equipped with a jointly surjective family of
36	relatively representable open immersions from representables.  The work done
37	here is the translation layer:
38	
39	1. **Size reduction / total functor** (`ZariskiDescent.GluedPoint`,
40	   `ZariskiDescent.gluedFunctor`): the values of `F` live in `Type 1`, so `F`
41	   cannot be fed to the mathlib theorem directly.  Instead we encode a point
42	   of the would-be total space over `T : Scheme` as a `Type 0` datum: a base
43	   morphism `a : T ⟶ S` together with a family of *classifying morphisms*
44	   `γ i : T|_{a⁻¹ U i} ⟶ Y i` into the local representing objects, compatible
45	   on overlaps as classified `F`-sections.  The bespoke sheaf axiom for `F`
46	   shows `GluedPoint T ≃ Σ (a : T ⟶ S), F(T, a)` (`ZariskiDescent.totalEquiv`),
47	   identifying `gluedFunctor` with the (large) total functor of `F`.
48	2. **Sheaf axiom** (`ZariskiDescent.isSheaf`): `gluedFunctor` is a sheaf for
49	   the big Zariski topology.  Covers by arbitrary jointly surjective open
50	   immersions are reduced to covers by opens of the target (the generated
51	   sieves agree), where the claim follows from the sheaf axiom of `F` through
52	   `totalEquiv`.
53	3. **Charts** (`ZariskiDescent.chart`): each `Y i` maps to `gluedFunctor` by
54	   sending `t : T ⟶ (Y i).left` to the point classified by the `F`-section
55	   that `t` represents; these are relatively representable open immersions
56	   (the pullback against a point `(a, x)` of `gluedFunctor` is the open
57	   subscheme `a⁻¹ U i ⊆ T`) and jointly surjective.
58	4. **Conclusion**: mathlib glues a scheme `Ŷ` with `gluedFunctor ≅ Hom(-, Ŷ)`;
59	   the tautological point of `Ŷ` gives the structure morphism `â : Ŷ ⟶ S`,
60	   and `totalEquiv` converts the absolute representability into
61	   `F.RepresentableBy (Over.mk â)`.
62	
63	## References
64	
65	Blueprint: `thm:representability_zariski_descent`, `def:zariski_sheaf_over`
66	(`blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`).
67	Source: EGA 0_I 4.5.4; Stacks 01JJ; [Nitsure] §1 (FGA Explained Ch. 5).
68	-/

9	/-!
10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
11	
12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
16	
17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
18	
19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
21	a sheaf**, not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302): a line
22	bundle on `C ×_k T` can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T` without
23	being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`, because the gluing data is a `Pic`-class
24	of the overlaps. Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
25	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
26	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
27	hypothesis.
28	
29	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
30	supplied:
31	
32	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
33	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
34	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
35	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
36	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
37	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
38	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
39	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
40	
41	## The site
42	
43	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
44	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
45	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
46	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
47	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
48	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
49	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
50	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
51	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
52	hypothesis.
53	
54	## Main definitions
55	
56	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
57	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
58	  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
59	  relative Picard presheaf.
60	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
61	  standalone statement about the underlying presheaf.
62	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C` — the set-valued functor
63	  `T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that the representability obligation is stated
64	  against, together with `picEtComparison C`, the canonical comparison
65	  `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` from the unsheafified functor.
66	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` — the sheaf property of `picEt`
67	  itself (the group structure forgotten), which is what a representing scheme
68	  must match.
69	
70	## References
71	
72	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Def. `df:Pfs` (the
73	étale-sheaf clause) and Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`), §4 Thm. `th:main`.
74	Blueprint: `def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification`,
75	`thm:rel_pic_etale_sheaf_group_structure`, `sec:fga_pic_setup`.
76	-/

/-! ## §3. Representability of the pulled-back absolute functor

`Scheme.{0}` has binary products (`Spec ℤ` is terminal, pullbacks exist), so
the forgetful functor `Over S ⥤ Sch` has the right adjoint `Over.star S`,
`Y ↦ (S ⨯ Y, fst)`.  The base change of the absolute Grassmannian to `S` is
`(Over.star S).obj Gr(d, r)`, and the adjunction transports the absolute
representability (`AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.represents`) to `Over S`. -/

/-- The merged absolute Grassmannian functor, restricted to `Over S` along the
forgetful functor, is representable by the base change
`(Over.star S).obj Gr(d, r) = (S ⨯ Gr(d, r), fst)` of the absolute
Grassmannian scheme. -/
noncomputable def prodRepresentableBy (S : Scheme.{0}) (d r : ℕ)
    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) :
    ((Over.forget S).op ⋙ AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.functor d r).RepresentableBy
      ((Over.star S).obj (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.scheme d r)) where
  homEquiv {T} :=
    ((Over.forgetAdjStar S).homEquiv T
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.scheme d r)).symm.trans
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.represents d r hd hdr).homEquiv
  homEquiv_comp {T T'} f g := by
    change (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.represents d r hd hdr).homEquiv
        (((Over.forgetAdjStar S).homEquiv _ _).symm (f ≫ g)) = _
    rw [Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm]
    exact (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.represents d r hd hdr).homEquiv_comp
      ((Over.forget S).map f) (((Over.forgetAdjStar S).homEquiv _ _).symm g)

/-! ## §4. Representability: trivialised and locally free cases -/

/-- **Representability of the relative Grassmannian, trivialised case**: for a
globally trivialised module `V ≅ O_S^r` on a locally noetherian `S` and
`1 ≤ d ≤ r`, the functor `Grass(V, d)` is representable by the base change
`S ⨯ Gr(d, r)` of the absolute Grassmannian.  Complete proof: transport the
representability of the pulled-back absolute functor
(`prodRepresentableBy`) along the comparisons `congrIso` and `freeCompare`. -/
theorem representable_of_iso_free {V : S.Modules} {r : ℕ}
    (e : V ≅ SheafOfModules.free (R := S.ringCatSheaf) (Fin r)) {d : ℕ}
    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) :
    ∃ (Y : Over S), Nonempty ((Scheme.Grassmannian V d).RepresentableBy Y) :=
  ⟨(Over.star S).obj (AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.scheme d r),
    ⟨(prodRepresentableBy S d r hd hdr).ofIso
      ((Scheme.Grassmannian.congrIso e d ≪≫ freeCompare d r).symm)⟩⟩

end Grassmannian

/-! ## §5. Zariski descent of representability (moved)

The definitions `overRes` / `overResHom` / `overResLE` / `IsZariskiSheafOver`
and the descent theorem `Scheme.representable_of_openCover`
(EGA 0_I 4.5.4; Stacks 01JJ) now live in
`AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/ZariskiDescentRepresentability.lean`, where the
theorem is **proved** (via mathlib's
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalRepresentability`, Stacks 01JJ, applied to the
small total functor of `F`). -/

/-! ## §6. Restriction of the Grassmannian to an open of the base
        exact congrArg (· ≫ (Scheme.Modules.pullback ψ.unop.left).map x.q)
          (restrictBase_naturality_core j V ψ.unop))

/-- **Local representability over a trivialising open**: over an open
`U ⊆ S` on which `V` trivialises, the restriction of the Grassmannian
functor to `Sch/U` is representable.  Complete proof: compose the
restriction comparison `restrictIso` with the trivialised case
`representable_of_iso_free` (the trivialisation index is re-normalised from
`ULift (Fin r)` to `Fin r` through the free functor). -/
theorem representable_restrict {V : S.Modules} {r : ℕ} (U : S.Opens)
    (e : (Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj V ≅
      SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{0} (Fin r)))
    {d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) :
    ∃ Y : Over U.toScheme,
      Nonempty (((Over.map U.ι).op ⋙ Scheme.Grassmannian V d).RepresentableBy Y) := by
  obtain ⟨Y, ⟨hY⟩⟩ := representable_of_iso_free
    (e ≪≫ (SheafOfModules.freeFunctor (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf)).mapIso
      (Equiv.toIso Equiv.ulift)) hd hdr
  exact ⟨Y, ⟨hY.ofIso (restrictIso U.ι V d).symm⟩⟩

/-- **The Grassmannian functor is a Zariski sheaf** ([Nitsure] §1; the
implicit locality behind the chart construction).  Families of rank-`d`
locally free quotients glue along an open cover of the parameter scheme:
the target sheaves glue by descent of sheaves of modules along the cover
(the `Scheme.Modules.glue` engine of `GlueDescent.lean` at the glue datum of
the cover), the quotient maps glue through the descent-equalizer lift
`Scheme.Modules.glueLift`, local freeness and epi-ness are local, and the
glued family is unique up to the equivalence `ker q = ker q'` because an
isomorphism of quotients commuting with the epimorphisms is unique when it
exists, so the local comparison isos satisfy the descent cocycle for free.
Proved in `GrassmannianZariskiSheaf.lean`
(`Scheme.grassmannian_isZariskiSheafOver`). -/
theorem isZariskiSheaf (V : S.Modules) (d : ℕ) :
    IsZariskiSheafOver (Scheme.Grassmannian V d) :=
  Scheme.grassmannian_isZariskiSheafOver V d

/-- **Representability of the Grassmannian** (`thm:grassmannian_representable`,
[Nitsure] §1 "Construction of Grassmannian", Exercise (2)): for a locally
noetherian `S`, a locally free `O_S`-module `V` of rank `r`, and `1 ≤ d ≤ r`,
the functor `Grass(V, d)` is representable by an `S`-scheme.  Proof: `V`
trivialises on an open cover of `S`; over each member the functor is
representable (`representable_restrict`, via the merged absolute chart
construction), and representability descends along the cover
(`Scheme.representable_of_openCover`) since the Grassmannian functor is a
Zariski sheaf (`isZariskiSheaf`). -/
theorem representable {V : S.Modules} {r : ℕ}
    (hV : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank V r) {d : ℕ}
    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdr : d ≤ r) :
    ∃ (Y : Over S), Nonempty ((Scheme.Grassmannian V d).RepresentableBy Y) := by
  obtain ⟨ι, U, hU, hloc⟩ := hV
  refine representable_of_openCover (Scheme.Grassmannian V d)
    (isZariskiSheaf V d) U hU (fun i => ?_)
  obtain ⟨e⟩ := hloc i
  exact representable_restrict (U i) e hd hdr

end Grassmannian
